newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT - Sabesp still a Flemings buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Sabesp still a Flemings buy.

text.p: Robert Fleming & Co Ltd said it reiterated its buy rating on Brazilian water and sewer utility Sabesp, which began trading last week on the Sao Paulo bolsa.

Flemings analyst Raphael Biderman said in a report, however, that he raised his price target for Sao Paulo city-owned Sabesp to a range between 360 reais and 375 reais from a previous target of 320 reais.

He cited Sabesp's announcement last Wednesday of a 9.8 percent rate hike for all customers. "The impact of a 9.8 percent tariff boost on a company with net revenue of 2.4 billion reais is obviously extremely significant," he wrote.
The company also had a 10-percent hike in labor costs, which represent 66 percent of its total costs, Biderman said.
But rising costs are unlikely to overshadow the rate hike because of a "leveraging effect" which will expand Sabesp' gross margin and gross profits, he said.

Due to the rate hike, Flemings has raised its 1997 earnings forecast for the firm to 382.2 million reais from 339 million reais and its 1998 earnings estimate to 755.6 million reais from 703.8 million reais, he added.

Meanwhile, Sao Paulo Hydraulic Resources Secretary Hugo Rosas said Sabesp plans to expand in Brazil and abroad into the privatization of other Latin American water firms, possibly with the help of a strategic partner.
"Both the expansion abroad and the addition of a strategic partner would be very positive developments," Biderman said.
